A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FP4DiT. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and additional experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization evaluations, ablations, generated-image comparisons and a 15-participant preference study, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, a 17-participant preference study and measured GPU layer latency.

M1.justification: The mixed FP formats, scale-aware AdaRound objective and gates, group-wise weight quantization, and online token-wise activation quantization remain unchanged. The CUDA timing implementation does not document a different quantization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain text-to-image evaluation using MS-COCO, the four HPSv2 categories and PixArt prompts, with PixArt-α, PixArt-Σ and Hunyuan. The COCO release/split revision changes the protocol within this coverage. ImageNet is discussed as prior work's setting, not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds Q-DiT at W4A8 and W4A6 for all three models and adds ViDiT-Q for Hunyuan, absent from v1 Tables 2 and 9. New Table 3 compares FP4DiT against these DiT-specific competitors in a preference study; the original Q-Diffusion/TFMQ-DM study remains in Table 4.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 change the reported calibration/evaluation data from COCO 2017 to COCO 2014, and Hunyuan evaluation from 3,000 to 5,000 images. v2 also introduces a 120-prompt, 17-participant study and controlled RTX 5080 layer-timing experiments. These establish reported protocol changes without establishing that every retained score was recomputed.

E4.justification: Figures 7–8 extend qualitative case comparisons concerning prompt adherence and image artifacts to additional competitors. Section 4.4 adds analysis of latency across FP/INT formats and activation precisions. Existing component, group-size, FP-format and calibration-budget ablations remain; the FP-format study moves from the appendix to Section 4.3.1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; additional participant counts concern evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 revises all 25 retained FID entries and adds eight comparator rows, while retained HPSv2 and CLIP values remain unchanged. FP4DiT's PixArt-α W4A8 FID changes from 46.18 to 30.37 under revised COCO conditions, not a demonstrated same-setting gain. New results include 52.14% and 45.00% preference shares in Table 3 and approximately 1.47–1.54× FP layer speedups in Table 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, the optimization objective, and both scale-dependence theorems and proofs are retained. The proof moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix A.1 without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims concerning W4A6/W4A8 FP quantization, GELU-sensitive mixed formats, scale-aware AdaRound, token-wise activations and reduced calibration cost. Additional comparisons support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds AdaLN/calibration-based explanations of why LLM quantization transfers imperfectly to DiTs and acknowledges small A6 latency overhead. It also strengthens v1's trade-off discussion into an overstated PixArt-Σ A6 interpretation: Table 2 still shows FID worsening from 31.58 at A8 to 42.21 at A6.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the CUDA 12.8/RTX 5080 timing setup but removes v1 Appendix B.2's detailed baseline adaptations and the direct FP4DiT repository link. Calibration hyperparameters, evaluation libraries, other hardware descriptions and the generic code/README statement remain. The removed link does not establish that code availability itself changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against LLM quantization through discussion of outliers, AdaLN compatibility and calibration costs, with new QuaRot, OWQ, AWQ, DuQuant and PB-LLM citations. It adds Q-DiT, clarifies HQ-DiT's class-conditional ImageNet scope, and removes the kernel-fusion reference.

P1.justification: Related-work, results and hardware prose is revised; the FP-format ablation moves into Section 4.3.1, supplementary quantitative discussion enters the main results, and appendix sections are reorganized. The overall introduction–method–results–conclusion sequence and most methodological prose remain.

P2.justification: The predominantly two-column design becomes a single-column layout with wrapped figures and extensively rearranged displays. v1's summary and supplementary benchmark tables become expanded v2 Table 2; new preference and latency tables appear, and Figures 7–8 gain comparators. Existing ablation figures move, while supplementary image examples are retained at reduced embedded resolution.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through more relevant competitors, another preference study and measured GPU layer latency, improving on v1's reliance on throughput specifications for runtime arguments. These gains are limited by removal of baseline implementation details and the code pointer, plus the overstated PixArt-Σ A6 interpretation. The timing evidence concerns selected layers, and revised FID scores use changed settings. Overall, the evidence supports a modest net improvement.
